NONE: › sometimes happy and sometimes sad
（情緒）波動的，時好時壞的
› sometimes successful and sometimes not successful
時好時壞的

example: She's been very up and down since her husband went into hospital.
自從丈夫住院以後，她的情緒波動很大。

NONE: › everywhere in a particular area, especially an area that stretches from north to south
到處，處處

example: Cities up and down the East Coast are preparing for the storm.
東海岸各地城鎮都在為迎接風暴做準備。
Cinemas up and down the country are reporting huge audiences for the film.
據報道，該影片在全國各地電影院的入座率都很高。

NONE: › If something, especially a system or a machine, is up and running it is operating.
（尤指系統或機器）運行，運轉

example: The engineer soon got the air-conditioning up and running again.
工程師很快就使空調重新運轉起來。

NONE: › available and ready to be won or taken
人人都可以爭取，供大家爭取，提供給任何人

example: There are hundreds of prizes up for grabs.
有幾百份獎品等著大家去拿。

NONE: › If a matter is up in the air, it is uncertain, often because other matters have to be decided first.
懸而未決

example: The whole future of the project is still up in the air.
這個企劃案前途未蔔。

NONE: › to take all the things that you own and go and live in a different place
遷居別處，搬家

example: This is the fourth time in five years that we've had to up sticks.
這已經是五年中我們第四次不得不搬家了。

NONE: › If you up the ante, you increase your demands or the risks in a situation in order to achieve a better result.
增加賭注；提高要求；提高風險
› in trouble
陷入困境；處於困境

example: If any more people resign, we'll be really up the creek.
如果再有更多的人辭職，我們真的就麻煩了。

NONE: › wasted or spoiled
浪費掉的；毀掉的，毀壞的

example: Peter lost his job so that was our holiday plans up the spout.
彼得丟了工作，我們的度假計劃也因此泡湯。

NONE: B1 used to say that something is less than or equal to but not more than a stated value, number, or level
接近於；至多
B1 also up until until
直到
B1 to be the responsibility of someone
是（某人）的職責
› to be doing something, often something bad or illegal, usually secretly
（通常指偷偷地）正在做（常指壞事或不法之事）

example: Up to two hundred people were on board the ship.
有將近200人搭乘了這艘船。
We can teach dancers up to intermediate level here.
我們這兒最高可以把舞蹈學員教到中級水準。
Up to yesterday, we had no idea where the child was.
直到昨天我們還不知道孩子的下落。
It's up to the manager to make the final decision.
這要由經理最後拍板。
She's up to no good (= doing something bad or forbidden) - you can always tell because she stays in her room.
她沒幹甚麽好事——你總會看出來的，因爲她老留在房間裡。
He looks very suspicious hanging around outside - I'm sure he's up to something.
他老在外邊徘徊，看上去很可疑——我敢肯定他正在做甚麽壞事。

NONE: › good enough for a particular activity
好得能勝任
› strong enough for a particular activity
強壯得能進行（某種活動）

example: He wants to compete at international level, but honestly I don't think he's up to it.
他想參加國際比賽，但說實話，我認爲他還達不到那個水準。
It was a serious fall - it'll be a while before you feel up to walking again.
摔得很嚴重——得過一陣子你才能行走。

NONE: B2 partly, or to a limited degree
在一定程度上

example: Of course there is some truth in all this, but only up to a point.
這當然有些道理，但僅在一定程度上。
The new traffic system worked up to a point, but it had its problems.
新的交通方案實行起來還相當有效，但仍有些問題。

NONE: B1 modern, recent, or containing the latest information
現代的；最近的；包含最新資訊的

example: We work hard to keep our database up to date.
我們花了很大力氣不斷更新資料庫。
[ before noun ] up-to-date information
最新资讯
See also
update verb

NONE: C2 reaching an acceptable standard
達到標準

example: Your last essay wasn't up to scratch/didn't come up to scratch.
你上一篇文章沒有達到要求。

NONE: › US informal as good as it should be; of an acceptable standard
達到可能實現的最好程度；達到可接受的標準

example: The phone system just wasn't up to snuff.
電話系統就是沒達到要求。

NONE: C1 If you are up to speed with a subject or activity, you have all the latest information about it and are able to do it well.
了解最新情況；跟上進度

example: We arranged for some home tutoring to get him up to speed with the other children in his class.
我們安排了一些家庭輔導，以幫助他跟上班裡其他孩子的進度。
Before we start the meeting I'm going to bring you up to speed with the latest developments.
在會議開始之前，我想先向大家介紹一下最新的進展。

NONE: › shouted or written on notices to show support
支援…，要求…（用於表示支持的口號或標語中）

example: Up with freedom, down with repression!
支援自由，反對鎮壓！

NONE: › used to show that you very much dislike someone or the things that someone has just said or done
（表示反感）去你的！
› Something that is done (up) to the hilt is done completely and without any limits
完全地，徹底地

example: The government is already borrowing up to the hilt.
政府已經完全靠借貸度日了。

NONE: › likely to achieve success soon or in the near future
有前途的
› An up-and-over door opens by being lifted and then sliding into a horizontal position as it rises.
（門）上提式開啓的
› in the direction of or relating to the parts of a country further from the coast, especially where there are few towns and people
向內陸地區（尤指人口稀少處）地，內陸地區的

example: We'll travel up-country by horse tomorrow.
我們明天騎馬向內陸地區出發。
Some people find up-country customs strange.
一些人認為內陸地區的風俗很奇怪。

NONE: › a woman's hairstyle in which the hair is arranged on top of the head, especially for a special occasion such as a wedding
高髻（一種將頭髮朝上梳並在頭頂盤成髻的髮型，尤其是在特殊場合如婚禮時梳的這種髮型）
› Up-tempo music has a fast beat.
（音樂）快節奏的；以快節奏
› modern
最新款的
› most recent; containing the most recent information
最近的；包含最新資訊的；時新的；即時的
› containing all the most recent information
最新的，最近的

example: Now we're going live to our reporter in Washington for up-to-the-minute news on the crisis.
現在我們將連線本台駐華盛頓的記者，現場報道關於該危機的最新消息。

NONE: › to be the type of thing that you are interested in or that you enjoy doing
合口味；為（某人）所喜愛

example: Kate loves dancing, so salsa lessons would be right up her alley.
凱特喜歡跳舞，所以薩爾薩舞蹈課正合她的口味。
